summary: Adolf Noreen was a linguist who studied at Uppsala University (~1871–1877) and under August Leskien (~1878–1879). He held a post at Uppsala University from around 1877 to 1919.

Adolf Schlagintweit worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He earned a Dr.med. from the University of Munich (~1846–1849), served there as Privatdozent in 1850, and was employed by the East India Company for exploration in 1854.

Linguist Adolf Tobler studied at the University of Zurich (1853–1854) and under Friedrich Christian Diez and Nikolaus Delius at the University of Bonn (1854–1857). He served at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1867 to 1910.

Adolfo Esteller y Melià was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University, under Robert Zimmermann, at Ignatius College, Valkenburg, and under Heinrich Lüders and Wilhelm Schulze at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and the Heras Institute.

Adolphe Pictet was a linguist who studied at Geneva, Paris, Humboldt University of Berlin under G. W. F. Hegel, Edinburgh, and London. He was a Privatdozent at the University of Geneva from 1840 to 1844.

Adolphe Regnier worked in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology, having studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held positions at Lycée Saint-Louis, Lycée Charlemagne, Collège de France, École Normale Supérieure, the Palace of Fontainebleau, and the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres.

Adoniram Judson Eaton was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Acadia University, Harvard University, Yale University, and the University of Leipzig. He held posts at Amherst Academy, Woonsocket High School, and McGill University.

Indologist Adriaan Scharpé studied at KU Leuven under Albert Joseph Carnoy and at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He served as a docent at Ghent University (1944–1979) and professor at the University of Amsterdam (1947–1978).

Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at the University of Auckland and the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger, and has held posts at the European School of Culture and Theology, Columbia International University Korntal, and the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation.
Adrien Barthélemy was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at INALCO and at EPHE under James Darmesteter, later teaching at both institutions from 1909 to 1929.

Adrienne Audrey G. Bennett was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She served as librarian for the Buddhist Society (1949–1952), editor of The Middle Way (1951–1952), and held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society (1956–1966).
Adrián Muñoz works in Indology and religious studies. He has held academic posts at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (attested 2011) and El Colegio de México (attested 2020).

Afeef Ahmed is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar studying as a Ph.D. candidate at Harvard University (attested 2024–2026), and has held a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar.

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and the University of Bonn (1995), and holds posts at the University of Warsaw (attested 2008, 2026).

Agathe Keller works in Indology and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD and habilitation at Paris Diderot University (2000) and has held positions at CNRS (from 2005, attested 2017), REHSEIS (attested 2006), and Paris Diderot University (attested 2017).

Agehananda Bharati was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and under Erich Frauwallner. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, University of Washington, and Syracuse University, among other visiting appointments.

Agnes Margrethe Agerschou was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Copenhagen (M.A., 1940) and worked as an assistant on the Critical Pāli Dictionary from 1940 to 1949.

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw and Nicolaus Copernicus University, later holding posts at Cornell University, the University of Warsaw, and the University of Hamburg.

Agvan Dorzhiev was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery and Drepung Gomang Dratsang, receiving the Geshe Lharampa degree. He founded Atsagat Datsan in 1913 and Datsan Gunzechoinei.

Ahmad Hasan Dani worked in archaeology and Indology, studying at Banaras Hindu University under A. S. Altekar, with Mortimer Wheeler, and at the University of London under K. de B. Codrington. He held posts at Dhaka, Peshawar, and Quaid-i-Azam universities.
